meaning:
Βαραββᾶς, -ᾶ, ὁ (Aram. בַּר־אַבָּא, lit., son of a father, i.e. accusative to Jerome, filius magistri),
Barabbas: Mat.27:16, 17 20, 21, 26, Mrk.15:7, 11 15, Luk.23:18, Jhn.18:40. (In Mat.27:16, some MSS. read Ἰησοῦν Β.; see WH, App., 19f.).†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: They had then a notable prisoner, called Barabbas.
There was one called Barabbas, bound with his fellow insurgents, men who in the insurrection had committed murder.
But they all cried out together, saying, “Away with this man! Release to us Barabbas!”—
Then they all shouted again, saying, “Not this man, but Barabbas!” Now Barabbas was a robber.
